column2: She saw sala, tala and tamala trees, nicula and lomaka, and other best of trees laden with fruit and flowers,
and occupied by chakoras, shataparnas, bhringarajas, parrots, cuckoos, kalavinkas, haritas, jivajivakas,
priyaputras, chataka birds and many other birds crying very sweetly, delightful to the ear;
and charming lakes with clear water, with water-lilies, white lotuses and lovely blue lotuses,
covered all around with kahlara and kamala flowers, with kadambas, chakravakas and water-cocks,
karandavas, cranes, swans, tortoises and madgus; filled all around with these and other water-dwellers.
Thus in due order she wandered in the forest with them. Seeing the lovely forest, supremely wonderful, with them,
her eyes bloomed with amazement, the excellent woman, and she spoke to Vayu, Kama and Vasanta, best of Brahmins:
All of you, each separately, give me help.
Having so spoken, then she, told "So be it" by the gods, Brahmins, replied: "Today I shall go where that sage stays.
Today I shall make him, the driver of the body's chariot with the horse-like senses yoked, a bad charioteer, with the reins thrown from his hand by the weapons of love.
Be it Brahma, or Janardana, or the dark-red Shiva, even so today I shall make a gap pierced by the arrows of love."
Having said so she went where the sage stayed, a hermitage where wild animals were quieted by the sage's austerity.
She stood on the river bank in the sweetness of male cuckoos' notes; staying but a moment, the excellent apsaras sang.
Then suddenly Vasanta (spring) made his force, the sweetness of cuckoos' calls, charming out of season.
The scent-bearing wind that dwells on Mount Malaya blew, dropping flowers, high and low, pure, slowly.
And Kama, holding flower-arrows, went near him and agitated the sage's mind too.
Then, hearing the sound of song, the sage, astonished, went where the fair-browed one was, tormented by love's arrows.
Seeing her, he said, eyes wide with wonder, his upper cloth slipped, disturbed, his body bristling:
Who are you, whose are you, fair-hipped, fortunate, sweetly smiling? You steal my mind, fair-browed; tell the truth, slender-waisted.
I am your servant, and I came for flowers. Give me a command quickly; what shall I do at your order?
Hearing her words he gave up composure, bewildered, took that young woman by the hand and entered his own hermitage.
Then Kama, Vayu and Vasanta, Brahmins, all went as they had come to heaven, their task done.
They went to Hari and reported her deed and his; hearing it, Shakra and the gods were pleased in mind.
And Kandu, entering the hermitage with her, made his own form supremely handsome, like Madana,
endowed with beauty and youth, very charming, with divine ornaments, of the appearance of sixteen years,
wearing divine garments, lovely, adorned with divine garlands and perfumes, furnished with all enjoyments, suddenly by the force of austerity.
Seeing his power she was greatly amazed, and saying "Ah, the power of his austerity," she was delighted.
Bathing, twilight worship, chanting, fire-offering, Vedic study, worship of deities, vows, fasting, restraints and meditation, best of sages —
abandoning these he played joyfully with her day and night, his heart possessed by love, and did not notice the decay of his austerity.
Twilights, nights, days, fortnights, months, seasons, solstices and years — he did not notice the time that had passed, his mind attached to objects.
And she, clever in the ways of love, Brahmins, in private chose him, the fair-hipped, skilled in prattle.
Thus Kandu stayed with her more than a hundred years in the valley of Mandara, the sage delighting in worldly pleasure.
She said to the fortunate one, "I wish to go to heaven; be gracious-faced, Brahmin; you ought to permit me."
Thus addressed by her, the sage, attached to her, said, "Stay a few days, good one."
Thus told, she enjoyed pleasures again with that great-souled one for a full hundred years.
Give me leave, revered one; I go to the abode of the gods. Told this by her, he again said, "Stay."
When more than a hundred years had again passed, the lovely-faced one said: "I go to heaven, Brahmin, charming with loving smiles."
Told so by her, the sage again said to the long-eyed one: "Stay here with me, fair-browed; you will go after a long time."
Fearing his curse, the fair-hipped one stayed with that sage again for two hundred years less a little.
When asked to go to the dwelling of the king of gods, the fortunate one was told "Stay" again and again by the slim woman.
Afraid of his curse, and by courtesy, the courteous one, knowing the pain of broken affection, did not leave the sage.
As he played with her day and night, the great sage's love was ever new, his mind attached to love.
Once the sage hastily came out of the hut; as he came out she, the auspicious, said: "Where is he going?"
Thus addressed by her he said, "The day has turned, auspicious one; I shall perform the twilight worship, otherwise the rite would lapse."
Then, laughing, delighted, she said to the great sage: "Today, knower of all dharma, has your day turned? Whom does this not amaze, that so much has gone?
You came in the morning, good one, to this auspicious river bank; I saw you, fair-hipped, and you entered my hermitage.
And this is the twilight; ah, it has changed. For what is this mockery? Tell me the true state."
You came at dawn, Brahmin; this is true, not false by me. But today, hundreds of years of that time have gone by for you.
Then the Brahmin, alarmed, asked the long-eyed one: "Tell me, timid one, what time has passed for me playing with you always?"
Nine hundred and seven years have passed, and six months, and three days more.
Timid one, is this true, or a joke, auspicious one? I think I have stayed here with you one day.
How, Brahmin, could I speak falsely here in your presence, especially as I have been asked by you, who follow the road?
Hearing her words, the sage, best of Brahmins, censured himself by himself: "Shame, shame on me, of improper conduct!
My austerities are destroyed, the wealth of the Brahman-knowers is destroyed; my discernment was stolen by someone; woman was made for delusion.
The Brahman, beyond the six waves, is to be known through self-conquest; shame on the great crocodile of desire by which I was brought to this state!
My vows, all the Vedas and all causes have been destroyed today by desire, by the road to the village of hell."

Having thus reproached himself by himself, the knower of dharma said to that apsaras who sat there: "Go, sinner, where you wish; what was to be done by you has been done, disturbing the king of gods with your gestures of love.
I do not turn you to ashes with the fire of fierce anger; I have lived with you in the friendship of the seventh step of the good.
Or what is your fault, or what can I do to you? The fault is mine alone, in that I was not a master of my senses.
As my austerities, intoxicated, were spent by you in seeking the pleasure of Shakra, so I am censured by the great delusion of vision."
While the sage thus spoke to the slender-waisted one, she began to tremble greatly, with dripping sweat.
The best of sages, in anger, said to her who was trembling, her body-vine dripping with sweat, the virtuous one: "Go, go."
She, thus rebuked, came out of the hermitage and, going through the sky, wiped her sweat with the shoots of trees.
The young woman went from tree to tree, wiping her limbs from which sweat was flowing, with high, red shoots.
The embryo that the sage had then placed in her body came out, in the form of sweat, with hair-bristling, from her limbs.
The trees took that embryo; the wind made it one; nourished by Soma and the cows, it then slowly grew.
A maiden named Marisha arose from the trees, lovely-eyed, the wife of the Prachetases, mother of Daksha, Brahmins.
And the revered Kandu, the best, his austerity exhausted, went to Vishnu's dwelling called Purushottama, Brahmins.
He saw the supreme field, granting liberation, rare on earth, on the shore of the southern ocean, granting the fruit of all desires,
very lovely, strewn with sand, adorned with groves of ketaki, strewn with many trees and creepers, with the cries of many birds, auspicious,
easy to move about everywhere, with flowers of all seasons, giving all happiness to men, blessed, a mine of all virtues,
earlier served by Bhrigu and others, the best of sages and Siddhas, and by Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakshas and others seeking liberation.
There he saw Hari adorned by all the gods, served by Brahmins and the other varnas dwelling in hermitages.
Seeing the field and the god Purushottama, the best of sages thought himself fulfilled.
There, one-pointed, he worshipped Hari, performing the chant called Brahmapara, with one-pointed mind, arms raised, that great yogi standing, best of sages.
Sage, we wish to hear the supreme, auspicious Brahmapara, by chanting which Kandu worshipped the god Keshava.

The beyond, the far; Vishnu, the farther shore of the shoreless, higher than the high, of the form of the Supreme Self; he is the Brahmapara, the farther shore of the farther, the highest of the highest, the shore beyond shore.
brahmapuran:178:115	He is the cause, though dependent on cause; the reason of that also, the reason of the reason of the highest; he is also the effect, and appears here in many forms with action and agent as everything.
brahmapuran:178:116	Brahman, lord, Brahman who has become all beings, Brahman, lord of creatures, the Imperishable; Brahman is the immutable, eternal, unborn Vishnu, unattached to all decay and the rest.
brahmapuran:178:117	As Brahman is imperishable and unborn, eternal, the Purushottama, so may passion and the other faults come to peace in me.
Hearing the sage's chant of Brahmapara, Brahmins, and knowing his supreme and very firm devotion, Purushottama,
with great love, the god, kind to devotees, Madhusudana, went near him and spoke,
in a voice deep as cloud, resounding the quarters as it were, mounted on Garuda, delight of Vinata's family, Brahmins:
Sage, say the supreme task that is in your mind; I have come as a boon-giver; choose a boon, good vow-holder.
Hearing these words of the god of gods, the discus-bearer, he opened his eyes and suddenly saw Hari before him,
like a flax flower, with lotus-petal eyes, conch, discus and mace in hand, wearing crown and armlets,
four-armed, noble-limbed, in yellow garments, lovely, bearing the Shrivatsa mark, adorned with a forest garland,
endowed with all marks, adorned with all jewels, his limbs anointed with divine sandal, adorned with divine garlands.
Then, filled with wonder, his body hairs bristling, he fell like a staff on the ground and made obeisance.
Today my birth is fruitful, today my austerity is fruitful, he said, tigers among sages, and began to praise him.

Narayana, Hari, Krishna, bearer of the Shrivatsa, lord of the world, seed of the world, abode of the world, witness of the world, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:129	Unmanifest, victorious, origin, Pradhana, Purushottama, lotus-eyed, Govinda, Lord of the world, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:130	Hiranyagarbha, Lord of Shri, Lord of the lotus, eternal, womb of the earth, steadfast, ruler, Hrishikesha, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:131	Without beginning or end, immortal, invincible, victory to you, best of victors, unconquered, undivided, Shri-Krishna, abode of Shri, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:132	Maker of rain and dharma, hard to cross, hard to approach, destroyer of the pain of suffering, Hari, lying on the waters, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:133	Protector of beings, unmanifest, lord of beings, undisturbed by the principles of beings, dwelling of beings, soul of beings, womb of beings, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:134	Sacrificer of sacrifice, bearer of sacrifice, giver of sacrifice, giver of fearlessness, womb of sacrifice, golden-limbed, Prishnigarbha, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:135	Knower of the field, bearer of the field, possessor of the field, destroyer of the field, maker of the field, master, soul of the field, free from the field, creator of the field, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:136	Abode of qualities, dwelling of qualities, refuge of qualities, bringer of qualities, enjoyer of qualities, delighting in qualities, renouncer of qualities, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:137	You are Vishnu, you Hari with the discus, you the victorious, you Janardana; you are what has been, you the vashat cry, you the future, you the lord who is.
brahmapuran:178:138	You are the maker of beings, you the unmanifest, you Bhava, you the supporter of beings; you are the god who is the origin of beings; they call you unborn, the Lord.
brahmapuran:178:139	You are Ananta, the grateful, you Prakriti, you Vrishakapi; you are Rudra, the unassailable, you the unfailing, you the Lord.
brahmapuran:178:140	You are Vishvakarma, the victorious, you Shambhu, you of the bull's form; you are Shankara, you Ushanas, you truth, you austerity, you the people.
brahmapuran:178:141	You are the conqueror of the universe, you bliss, you refuge, you the imperishable; you are Shambhu, you the Self-born, you the eldest, you the supreme goal.
brahmapuran:178:142	You are the Sun, you Om, you the life-breath, you the destroyer of darkness; you are Parjanya, you the renowned, you the Creator, you the lord of gods.
brahmapuran:178:143	You are the Rik, Yajus and Sama, you the Self, the esteemed; you are Agni, you the wind, you the waters, you the earth.
brahmapuran:178:144	You are the creator, and likewise the enjoyer, the priest, the oblation, the sacrifice; you are the lord, the all-pervading, the best, the lord of the world, Achyuta.
brahmapuran:178:145	You are all-seeing, glorious, you the subduer of all, destroyer of enemies; you are day, and you night, the wise call you the year.
brahmapuran:178:146	You are time, you the kala and kashtha, you the muhurta, moment and instant; you are the child, you the old, you the male, female and neuter.
brahmapuran:178:147	You are the womb of the universe, you the eye, you the immovable, you of pure fame; you are eternal, you unconquered, you Upendra, you the best.
brahmapuran:178:148	You are the giver of all happiness to the universe, you the limb of the Veda, you the imperishable; you are the knower of the Veda, you the supporter, you the disposer, you the composed.
brahmapuran:178:149	You are the ocean from the root, you the supporter, you Punarvasu, you the physician, you the steadfast self, you the one beyond the senses' range.
brahmapuran:178:150	You are the leader, the chief of the village, you Suparna, you the primal; you are the collection, you the very great, you the steadfast self, you Achyuta.
brahmapuran:178:151	You are Yama and the restraint, you the tall, you the four-armed; you alone are the inner self of food, you are called the Supreme Self.
brahmapuran:178:152	You are the teacher, you the greatest teacher, you the left, you the right-circling; you are the pippala, you the inaccessible, you the manifest, you the Prajapati.
brahmapuran:178:153	You are golden-naveled, the god, the moon, the Prajapati; of indescribable body, you are Yama, you the foe of the Asuras.
brahmapuran:178:154	You are the god Sankarshana, you the doer, you the eternal; you are Vasudeva of immeasurable soul, you alone are free of qualities.
brahmapuran:178:155	You are the eldest, the most excellent, you the patient, Madhava; you are the thousand-headed god, you the unmanifest with a thousand eyes,
brahmapuran:178:156	you the god with a thousand feet, you Virat, you lord of gods; you alone remain beyond, god of gods, ten fingers' breadth (beyond).
brahmapuran:178:157	What has been is said to be you alone, the Purusha, the best of Shakra's; what is to be is you, the Lord; you are truth, and you immortality.
brahmapuran:178:158	From you this world grows; you are greater, unsurpassed; you the elder Purusha, and you, god, stand tenfold.
brahmapuran:178:159	The universe is a fourth part; the immortal in heaven is nine parts; nine parts in the atmosphere, Paurusheya, eternal.
brahmapuran:178:160	Two parts are on earth, and a fourth also came to be here; from you sacrifices arise, cause of the world's rain.
brahmapuran:178:161	From you Virat arose; the Purusha in the world's heart surpasses beings in brilliance, fame and fortune.
brahmapuran:178:162	From you came the gods' food, the sprinkled ghee; from you the village and forest herbs, beasts and deer and the rest.
brahmapuran:178:163	Intent on the object of meditation, you made the herbs; you, god of gods, seven-mouthed, named Time, of blazing form.
brahmapuran:178:164	All this world, moving and unmoving, mobile and immobile, from you all this was born, and in you all is established.
brahmapuran:178:165	You are Aniruddha, you Madhava, you Pradyumna, foe of the Asuras; god, best of all gods, refuge of all worlds,
brahmapuran:178:166	save me, lotus-eyed Narayana; salutation to you; salutation to you, revered Vishnu; salutation to you, Purushottama.
brahmapuran:178:167	Salutation to you, lord of all worlds; salutation to you, dwelling of Kamala; abode of qualities, salutation to you; salutation to you, mine of qualities.
brahmapuran:178:168	Vasudeva, salutation to you; salutation to you, best of gods; Janardana, salutation to you; salutation to you, eternal.
brahmapuran:178:169	Salutation to you, attainable by yogis, abode of yoga; lord of cattle, lord of Shri, Vishnu, salutation to you; lord of the Maruts.
brahmapuran:178:170	Lord of the world, begetter of the world, salutation to you, lord of the knowers; lord of heaven, salutation to you; salutation to you, lord of the earth.
brahmapuran:178:171	Salutation to you, slayer of Madhu; salutation to you, lotus-eyed; slayer of Kaitabha, salutation to you; Subrahmanya, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:172	Salutation to you, great Fish, bearer of the Veda on your back, Achyuta; churner of the sea waters, delighter of the lotus-born (Brahma).
brahmapuran:178:173	Horse-headed, with great snout, great-bodied Purusha, slayer of Madhu and Kaitabha, horse-faced, salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:174	To you for the great tortoise form, and for lifting the earth, bearing the mountain, to the great Tortoise salutation.
brahmapuran:178:175	Salutation to the great Boar, who lifted the earth; salutation to the primal Boar, of universal form, the Creator.
brahmapuran:178:176	Salutation to the Infinite, the subtle, the chief and the excellent, whose form is the atom, attainable by yogis; salutation to you.
brahmapuran:178:177	Salutation to him, cause of causes, dwelling in the conduct of the lords of yogis, hard to know, reclining on the bed of the great serpent's daughter-(offspring) on the Milk-ocean, to you adorned with golden jewelled earrings, salutation.
brahmapuran:178:178	Thus praised, then Madhava, pleased, said: Say quickly, best of sages, what you wish from me."

In this worldly existence, lord of the world, hard to cross, hair-raising, impermanent, full of sorrow, like a plantain leaf,
brahmapuran:178:180	without refuge, without support, unsteady as a water bubble, full of all calamities, hard to cross and extremely terrible,
brahmapuran:178:181	I have wandered a very long time deluded by your maya, and with mind attached to objects I do not reach its end.
brahmapuran:178:182	Today, lord of gods, afflicted by the fear of worldly existence, I have come to you for refuge, Krishna; lift me from the ocean of existence.
brahmapuran:178:183	I wish to go to your supreme eternal state, lord of gods, by your grace, hard to obtain for those who return.

You are my devotee, best of sages; worship me constantly; by my grace you will certainly obtain the liberation you wish.
brahmapuran:178:185	My devotees, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, women, and those born of Shudra and lowest classes attain supreme success; what then of you, best of Brahmins?
brahmapuran:178:186	Even a dog-cooker who is my devotee, with proper faith, attains the success he wishes; what to say of others there?
